name: Yurumanguí
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct isolate known only from an 18th-c. wordlist (analyzed by Rivet 1942, Ortiz 1945); no phonological description of stress can exist.

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2019. Notes on Yurumanguí grammar and lexicon. LIAMES 19: e019015, 1-25. doi:10.20396/liames.v19i0.8656013
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 3 (pp. 4-5) 'Some regularities in and notable features of the transcription' covers only letter inventory and syllable structure; p. 3: 'I shall make no attempt to reconstruct an approximate pronunciation of the words collected by Romero or to make principled inferences about Yurumanguí phonology. The data seem too inconsistently transcribed..'; p. 11 the only remark on the accent marks: 'The fact that the final <-e> frequently bears a diacritic may suggest that one is dealing with a separate pronoun forming a phonological word of itself.'

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F.H. with Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, pp. 60-61 (sec. on Yurumanguí)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100.A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l)
sources.harvard_location: Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100 .A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l
sources.note: The standard modern overview of the Yurumanguí material; the only unread treatment by a specialist that might comment on Romero's accent marks (unlikely to state a stress rule, but would close the file).

sources.citation: Poser, William J. 1992. The Salinan and Yurumanguí data in Language in the Americas. IJAL 58(2): 202-229 (author's preprint)
sources.note: Nothing on Yurumanguí stress; the single 'stress' passage concerns Salinan (Mason's notebooks). Yurumanguí section (5) is about Greenberg's/Rivet's morphological segmentations.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1942. Un dialecte hoka colombien: le Yurumangí. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 34: 1-59. doi:10.3406/jsa.1942.2334
sources.note: Nothing. pp. 9-10 only say Romero 'a noté avec soin les sons' in Spanish spelling and that Rivet re-transcribes 'en notation phonétique' with the original in brackets; the whole 59-page scanned has no mention of accent/stress (accent, tonique, pénultième, oxyton: 0 hits). Romero's original spellings carry sporadic, uncommented acute accents, mostly word-final (lamá, chumá, acá, aicán, auciá, calumá, coguá, cuatuamé).

tone.says: Not re-read here; our reader's note on a work listed here (full scan read) says the article has no mention of accent, stress or tone -- Rivet only re-transcribes Romero's Spanish-orthography forms 'en notation phonetique'; the open copy adds access, not tone content.

sources.note: Phonology paragraph summarises Urban 2019 (absent letters, closed syllables rare); nothing on stress. Vocabulary table from Ortiz 1946 shows the sporadic final acutes (lamá, acá, aicán, auciá).

sources.citation: Constenla Umaña, Adolfo. 1991. Las lenguas del área intermedia: introducción a su estudio areal. San José: Editorial de la Universidad de Costa Rica, p. 53

sources.note: Typological notes on Yurumanguí cited by Urban 2019; Constenla codes accent type for Intermediate-Area languages and may say whether anything can be said for Yurumanguí.
